description_full: MSCI Inc., together with its subsidiaries, provides research-based data, analytics, and indexes, supported by advanced technology worldwide. The Index segment provides indexes for use in various areas of the investment process, including indexed financial products, such as ETFs, mutual funds, annuities, futures, options, structured products, and over-the-counter derivatives; performance benchmarking; portfolio construction and rebalancing; and asset allocation, as well as licenses GICS and GICS Direct. The Analytics segment offers risk management, performance attribution and portfolio management content, application, an integrated view of risk and return service, and an analysis of market, credit, liquidity, counterparty, and climate risk across asset classes; managed services, including consolidation of client portfolio data, review and reconciliation of input data and results, and customized reporting; and HedgePlatform to measure, evaluate, and monitor the risk of hedge fund investments. The Sustainability and Climate segment provides products and services that help institutional investors understand how ESG impacts the long-term risk and return of their portfolio and individual security-level investments; and data, ratings, research, and tools to assist investors navigate increasing regulation. The All Other  Private Assets segment comprises private credit, real estate and infrastructure data, benchmarks, return-analytics, climate assessments and market insights; business intelligence to real estate owners, managers, developers, and brokers; and offers investment decision support tools for private capital. The Private Capital Solutions segment offers tools to help private asset investors across mission-critical workflows, such as sourcing terms and conditions, evaluating operating performance, managing risk and other activities supporting private capital investment. MSCI Inc. was incorporated in 1998 and is based in New York, New York.

financial_summary: MSCI Inc. is a large-cap financial services business with a $47.1B market cap on $3.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years and +11% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 40% against a 10% cost of capital — a 30-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $1.5B in free cash flow — roughly 49 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.32× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.3× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 8.2×.

Management returns a meaningful 6.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 3.7% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.1× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 55% operating margin runs 26pp above the Financial Services median (29%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 2.11x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+2.1% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.02 across 514 companies in the universe; the top four hold 20% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 3% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 30% and a beta of 1.14, it moves roughly with the market.
Liquidity is deep, with about $302.0M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 32% in the 2020 crash, 36% in the 2022 bear market and 68% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $382 (margin of safety -72%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 32%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $275 to $533 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Financial Services peers: P/E 34.8 vs 12.3, EV/EBITDA 26.4 vs 10.6 and P/FCF 30.4 vs 13.0 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 9% above its 10-year median.
The 17 covering analysts target $686 on average, 4% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 19.2% annual cash-flow growth, 9pp more than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 40% clears the cost of capital of 9.5% by 30pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.56).
It converts 49% of revenue into free cash flow.
hlth: Goodwill makes up 51% of assets, a soft asset exposed to impairment.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 11.7% over 3 years, 13.1% over 5 years and 11.3% over 10 years.
At current returns, reinvesting 5% of profits supports about 2.1% a year of fundamental growth, too little to drive meaningful growth.
Analysts expect 13.9% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 3.7%, and institutions hold 96%.
Insider trading is two-way: 8 purchases and 3 sales over the past year, net $1.2M bought.
It returns 6.5% a year to shareholders (5.3% in buybacks and 1.2% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 2.8% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 11 consecutive years, raising it 17.7% a year over the last five.
people: With about 6,259 employees, each generates about $501K of revenue, in line with the Financial Services median, and revenue has grown 10.9% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $248K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.7M (7x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores poorly (8/10, lower is better).
